metadata.notes: AI Command Center chat webhook. After import: click this module, create a new webhook, name it 'AI Command Center Chat Webhook', copy the URL.

Shared AI engine for agency staff and authenticated employers. The Worker sends role-scoped context, while the thread ID isolates memory per user. After import: connect your Make AI Provider connection (same one used by your other AI scenarios).

Return the AI Agent's Response directly. For actions, the agent must respond with one valid JSON object: {"reply":"...","actions":[{"type":"website_api_action",...}]} or a navigation/applicant action. For no-action replies, plain text is fine. The Worker validates role, route, record scope, and payload, then asks the signed-in user to confirm before sending the action through the website API.

notes: Helped - AI Command Center - Import-ready blueprint.
1. WEBHOOK: Click Module 1, create a new webhook named 'AI Command Center Chat Webhook', copy its URL.
2. AI AGENT: Click Module 2, connect your Make AI Provider connection.
3. WEBHOOK RESPONSE: Map Body directly to Module 2 > Response and set Status to 200.
4. WORKER SECRET: npx wrangler secret put MAKE_AI_COMMAND_CENTER_WEBHOOK_URL (paste the webhook URL).
5. ACTIVATE: Toggle the scenario ON and keep webhook processing immediate (Sequential processing off).
The Worker sends { type, scenario, systemPrompt, userPrompt, messages, context }.
The AI agent uses 1.systemPrompt (role-scoped data + instructions) and 1.userPrompt + conversation history. Thread memory is isolated by scenario and authenticated user ID.

The webhook response returns Module 2's Response directly. Plain text is fine for chat-only replies. Whenever Module 2 proposes any action, it must return one valid JSON object shaped as {"reply":"...","actions":[...]} without Markdown fences. The Worker validates actions against the signed-in role and website API allowlist, then the portal shows the request and payload and requires the user to confirm before execution. This is a permissioned website action interface, not unrestricted computer or source-code control.
